hypothesis: P1's function.zip ships no usable Python bytecode: 149 .pyc whose source-mtime headers do not match the 2026-01-01 stamp the build gives every .py, and no .pyc at all for most modules. /var/task is read-only, so every cold start (and every SnapStart snapshot init) compiles every imported module from source and cannot cache it. Shipping complete unchecked-hash bytecode cuts the cold `imports` phase, and therefore Init Duration and the start of the background model load, with no change to answers, warm inference or restore.

conclusion_template: Complete unchecked-hash bytecode halves the cold imports phase on every CPU part Lambda gave us (CPU part 0xd40 as read from /proc/cpuinfo, n=49/52: {cold_imports_0xd40_ctl:.3f} -> {cold_imports_0xd40_pyc:.3f} s, delta {cold_imports_0xd40_d:+.3f} s, 95% CI [{cold_imports_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {cold_imports_0xd40_hi:+.3f}]; 0xd0c and 0xd4f the same direction in every shared round/part cell; all 12 shared cells below 0, with 5 sparse unmatched cells reported separately) and Init Duration by {cold_report_init_duration_0xd40_d:+.3f} s on 0xd40. Mechanism confirmed in-function: ctl recompiles all 153-157 task-root modules from source in every environment (0 usable .pyc), pyc recompiles 1 (the e6_entry wrapper itself). The cold first request does NOT improve: on 0xd40 first_request_total delta {cold_first_request_total_0xd40_d:+.3f} s, CI [-0.098, +0.079]. On 0xd0c (n=5/3 only) it is -0.685 s, CI [-1.168, -0.322]; on 0xd4f (n=6/5) +0.047 s, CI [-0.271, +0.250]. That is no consistent improvement across parts. The reason: the on-demand load runs in PR #77's background thread and the request waits for the ~25 s S3 download, which starts after imports either way; the saved ~0.37 s goes back into wait_for_load (weight_download on pyc +0.30 s, CI [{cold_weight_download_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {cold_weight_download_0xd40_hi:+.3f}], a download that starts earlier and ends at the same time: import_total + weight_download p50 25.75 vs 25.68 s). Billed cold duration is unchanged (REPORT Billed Duration includes Init; the Init saved is spent waiting for the load inside Duration). SnapStart snapshot init imports also halve on both CPU parts Lambda prepared snapshots on, each record bound to the CPU part in its own log stream (0xd40 {snapshot_imports_0xd40_ctl:.3f} -> {snapshot_imports_0xd40_pyc:.3f} s, n={snapshot_imports_0xd40_n}; 0xd0c {snapshot_imports_0xd0c_ctl:.3f} -> {snapshot_imports_0xd0c_pyc:.3f} s, n={snapshot_imports_0xd0c_n}; every delta beyond the control spread across published versions; 12/12 records linked, 0 missing, 0 ambiguous), but that is publish time, not restore latency: restore first request total delta {restore_first_request_total_0xd40_d:+.3f} s, CI [{restore_first_request_total_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {restore_first_request_total_0xd40_hi:+.3f}] (0xd40 only). Warm inference unchanged ({warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_d:+.4f} s, CI [{warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_lo:+.4f}, {warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_hi:+.4f}]). Answers: 420/420 pyc answers bit-identical to ctl for the same request and CPU part, and every answer P1's reference covers is bit-identical to it. Recommendation: adopt (no cost, +7 MB zip / +19 MB unzipped of the 250 MB limit, ~9 MB less peak memory) as hygiene; it pays off only where imports are on the request path, i.e. after a change that overlaps or removes the download (E4, E5, E9 or a combined ladder rung), so R should re-measure it there rather than credit it to the current baseline.
